metadata.note: A second, separate historical Houston-Dallas corridor: the Trinity and Brazos Valley Railway, reorganized in 1905 as the jointly-owned Burlington-Rock Island Railroad (Colorado & Southern/Chicago, Burlington & Quincy plus Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific). Extended from Mexia to Houston and from Teague to Waxahachie in 1907, giving a Houston-Dallas-Fort Worth route distinct from the older Houston and Texas Central line further west (see houston_texas_central.geojson). The Sam Houston Zephyr, Texas's first diesel-electric streamliner, ran this route from Oct 1 1936 until discontinued in 1966 -- again well before Amtrak (1971), so no direct Houston-Dallas passenger train exists today. Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation (Houston-Centerville-Teague-Corsicana-Waxahachie-Dallas-Fort Worth), straight-line segments between towns documented on the T&BV/BRI corridor -- NOT digitized from period track maps, so curvature within each town-to-town segment is still schematic rather than surveyed. Frequencies are estimated/unsourced except where noted; the Sam Houston Zephyr's average speed is a rough estimate since no confirmed detailed timetable was found.
sources: https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/burlington-rock-island-railroad (Trinity & Brazos Valley chartered 1902, Cleburne-Mexia by 1904; Colorado & Southern acquired 1905 with half interest to Rock Island; Mexia-Houston and Teague-Waxahachie completed 1907; original Cleburne-Mexia segment abandoned in stages 1932-1942, unrelated to the Houston-Dallas trunk modeled here)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Houston_Zephyr (jointly operated by Burlington-Rock Island; launched Oct 1 1936 as first diesel-electric streamliner in the Southwest/Texas; 283-mile Houston-Fort Worth route via Teague, Corsicana, Waxahachie, Dallas; original 3-car trainset destroyed by fire Dec 19 1944, service continued with replacement equipment; discontinued 1966)

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.ownership_split_correction: 2026-08-30: the Sam Houston Zephyr was drawn 1936-1966 as a single Burlington-Rock Island feature, but the Burlington-Rock Island Railroad was dissolved in 1965. Split at 1965 into two features sharing identical geometry (Rule 4): sam-houston-zephyr keeps the BRI for 1936-1965, sam-houston-zephyr-successor carries 1965-1966. The successor's company attribution is an inference and is flagged as such in its segment sources. Source: research/branches/chicago_burlington_and_quincy_railroad.txt, EXISTING LAYER CHECK.

segments.note: Launched Oct 1 1936, first diesel-electric streamliner in Texas; original 3-car trainset destroyed by fire Dec 19 1944, service continued under the same name with replacement equipment. This segment now ends 1965, when the Burlington-Rock Island Railroad was DISSOLVED and its property divided between the Fort Worth and Denver and the Rock Island. The train itself ran on to 1966 -- see the successor feature sam-houston-zephyr-successor, which carries that year. Corrected 2026-08-30 from an earlier single 1936-1966 span that drew one year under a company that no longer existed; single daily round trip, frequency approximate/unsourced
sources: Segment-level: the 1965 end year is the Burlington-Rock Island's dissolution, per the Texas State Historical Association Handbook of Texas, 'Burlington-Rock Island Railroad'. The 1936 start and the headway are NOT sourced at segment level.

segments.note: The Sam Houston Zephyr's final year. The Burlington-Rock Island was dissolved in 1965 and its property split between the Fort Worth and Denver and the Rock Island, so the 1965-66 train did NOT run under the Burlington-Rock Island name. WHICH successor actually operated it is NOT ESTABLISHED: the Fort Worth and Denver is the likelier of the two (it took the Burlington side of the property and the train was a Burlington-branded Zephyr), but no source consulted names the operator for these years. Treat the company attribution on this feature as unverified. Discontinued 1966; single daily round trip, frequency approximate/unsourced
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the 1965 dissolution and the 1966 discontinuance are both sourced below, but no source consulted names WHICH successor ran the train in 1965-1966. The Fort Worth and Denver attribution is an inference, not a checked fact.
